article_title: Performance evaluation of large language models on Korean medical licensing examination: a three-year comparative analysis.
citation: Kim Hyun Jin, Jung Kiwook, Shin Sunghwan, Lee Wookeun, Lee Jun Hyung, Park Hee Sue, Choi Qute. (2025). Performance evaluation of large language models on Korean medical licensing examination: a three-year comparative analysis. Scientific Reports. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-20066-x
title: KMLE 2022–2024 evaluation dataset of 942 Korean-language questions with physician-sourced images
description: A benchmark dataset of Korean Medical Licensing Examination questions from three consecutive years used to evaluate LLM medical knowledge in a non-English context. It contains "317 questions from 2022, 314 questions from 2023, and 311 questions from 2024, totaling 942 questions", spanning text-only and image-based A-type and R-type formats. Because the examination institute releases no official images, two licensed physicians independently sourced clinically relevant, de-identified images from open-access medical education resources; questions were preserved in their original Korean format and classified into seven medical specialties with an inter-annotator Cohen's kappa of 0.938.
requirements: Questions are sourced from publicly available KMLE materials released by the Korea Health Personnel Licensing Examination Institute (https://www.kuksiwon.or.kr)
constraints: Multimedia questions containing video or audio were excluded
Official images are not released by the institute, so images were physician-sourced rather than original exam images
target_learners: Medical school graduates and fourth-year students preparing for the Korean Medical Licensing Examination
target_learning_goals: Foundational medical knowledge and clinical skills assessed for medical licensure in Korea
examples: Automated API-based testing of GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Gemini 1.5 Pro with zero temperature and a new session per problem
